verses.38:14: Therefore prophesy, son of man, and say to Gog, 'Thus says the Lord: In that day, when My people Israel are settled in peace, shall you not be roused?
verses.38:15: And you shall come from your place out of the uttermost north, and many nations with you, all of them riders on horses, a great company and a mighty host,
verses.38:16: and you shall go up against My people Israel like a cloud to cover the land. It shall be in the last days, and I will bring you up against My land, so that all the nations may know Me, when I am sanctified in you before them.
verses.38:17: Thus says the Lord, the Lord to Gog: You are he of whom I spoke in former days by the hand of My servants the prophets of Israel, in those days and years, that I would bring you against them.
verses.38:18: And it shall come to pass in that day, in the day when Gog comes against the land of Israel, says the Lord, the Lord, that My fury shall arise,
verses.38:19: and My jealousy. In the fire of My wrath I have spoken: Surely in that day there shall be a great earthquake upon the land of Israel,
verses.38:20: and the fish of the sea, and the birds of heaven, and the beasts of the field, and all the creeping things that creep upon the earth, and all the people who are upon the face of the earth shall be shaken at the presence of the Lord; and the mountains shall be rent apart, and the ravines shall fall, and every wall shall fall to the ground.
verses.38:21: And I will summon against it even every terror, says the Lord; every man's sword shall be against his brother.
verses.38:22: And I will judge him with death and with blood, and with flooding rain and hailstones; and I will rain fire and brimstone upon him, and upon all those with him, and upon the many nations with him.
verses.38:23: And I shall be magnified and sanctified and glorified, and I shall be made known in the sight of many nations; and they shall know that I am the Lord.'"
verses.39:1: "And you, son of man, prophesy against Gog, and say, 'Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am against you, Gog, the prince of Rosh, Meshech, and Tubal;
verses.39:2: and I will gather you and guide you, and I will bring you up from the uttermost north, and I will lead you up upon the mountains of Israel.
verses.39:3: And I will destroy your bow from your left hand and your arrows from your right hand, and I will cast you down upon the mountains of Israel;
verses.39:4: and you shall fall, you and all those around you, and the nations that are with you shall be given to multitudes of birds; to every bird and to all the beasts of the field I have given you to be devoured.
verses.39:5: Upon the face of the field you shall fall, for I have spoken, says the Lord.
verses.39:6: And I will send fire upon Gog, and the islands shall be inhabited in peace, and they shall know that I am the Lord.
verses.39:7: And My holy name shall be made known in the midst of My people Israel, and My holy name shall not be profaned any more; and the nations shall know that I am the Lord, the Holy One in Israel.
verses.39:8: Behold, it is coming, and you shall know that it shall be, says the Lord, the Lord; this is the day of which I spoke.
verses.39:9: And those who dwell in the cities of Israel shall go out and make fire with the weapons—shields and pikes and bows and arrows and hand-staves and lances—and they shall burn fire with them for seven years;
verses.39:10: and they shall by no means take wood from the field, nor shall they cut down any from the forests, for they shall burn the weapons with fire; and they shall plunder those who plundered them, and despoil those who despoiled them, says the Lord.
verses.39:11: And it shall come to pass in that day that I will give Gog a renowned place, a burial place in Israel, the burial ground of those who came near the sea, and they shall wall around the mouth of the ravine;
verses.39:12: and there they shall bury Gog and all his multitude, and it shall be called Te, the Burial Ground of Gog. And the house of Israel shall bury them, that the land may be cleansed in seven months,
verses.39:13: and all the people of the land shall bury them; and it shall be a renown to them in the day that I am glorified, says the Lord.
verses.39:14: And they shall set apart men continually to pass through the land to bury those who remain upon the face of the earth, to cleanse it after the seven months, and they shall make search.
verses.39:15: And everyone who passes through the land and sees a man's bone shall build a marker beside it, until the buriers bury it in Gai, the Burial Ground of Gog;
verses.39:16: for indeed the name of the city is Polyandrion; and the land shall be cleansed.'
verses.39:17: And you, son of man, say, 'Thus says the Lord: Speak to every winged bird and to all the beasts of the field, "Gather yourselves and come; gather from all around to My sacrifice, which I have sacrificed for you, a great sacrifice upon the mountains of Israel, and you shall eat flesh and drink blood.
verses.39:18: You shall eat the flesh of giants, and drink the blood of the princes of the earth—rams and calves and goats, and all the calves are fatted.
verses.39:19: And you shall eat fat to fullness, and drink blood to drunkenness, from My sacrifice which I have sacrificed for you.
verses.39:20: And you shall be filled at My table with horse and rider, with giant and every man of war," says the Lord.
verses.39:21: And I will set My glory among you, and all the nations shall see My judgment which I have executed, and My hand which I have brought upon them.
verses.39:22: And the house of Israel shall know that I am the Lord their God from this day and onward.
verses.39:23: And all the nations shall know that because of their sins the house of Israel was led captive, because they broke faith with Me; and I turned My face away from them and delivered them into the hands of their enemies, and they all fell by the sword.
verses.39:24: According to their uncleannesses and according to their lawless deeds I dealt with them, and I turned My face away from them.
verses.39:25: Therefore thus says the Lord, the Lord: Now I will turn back the captivity in Jacob, and I will have mercy upon the house of Israel, and I will be zealous for My holy name.
verses.39:26: And they shall bear their dishonor and the unrighteousness which they committed, when they are settled upon their land in peace, and there shall be no one to make them afraid,
verses.39:27: when I bring them back from the nations and gather them out of the countries of the nations; and I shall be sanctified in them in the sight of the nations.
verses.39:28: And they shall know that I am the Lord their God, when I appear to them among the nations.
verses.39:29: And I will no longer turn My face away from them, because I have poured out My fury upon the house of Israel, says the Lord, the Lord.'"
verses.40:1: And it came to pass in the twenty-fifth year of our captivity, in the first month, on the tenth day of the month, in the fourteenth year after the city was captured, on that very day the hand of the Lord came upon me, and He brought me
verses.40:2: in a vision of God into the land of Israel, and He set me on an exceedingly high mountain, and upon it was like the structure of a city directly opposite.
verses.40:3: And He brought me in there, and behold, a man, and his appearance was like the appearance of gleaming bronze, and in his hand was a builders' cord and a measuring reed; and he was standing at the gate.
verses.40:4: And the man said to me, "Have you seen, son of man? See with your eyes and hear with your ears, and set upon your heart all that I show you, for you have come in here that I might show them to you; and you shall show all that you see to the house of Israel."
verses.40:5: And behold, there was an enclosing wall on the outside of the house all around, and in the hand of the man was a measuring reed of six cubits, each a cubit and a handbreadth; and he measured the outer wall, its width equal to the reed, and its height equal to the reed.
verses.40:6: And he entered the gate facing toward the east by seven steps, and he measured the vestibule of the gate as equal to the reed,
verses.40:7: and the side chamber equal to the reed in length and equal to the reed in width, and the vestibule between the side chambers six cubits; and the second side chamber equal to the reed in width and equal to the reed in length, and the vestibule five cubits;
verses.40:8: and the third side chamber equal to the reed in width and equal to the reed in length,
verses.40:9: and the vestibule of the gateway near the vestibule of the gate eight cubits, and the posts two cubits; and the vestibules of the gate were on the inside,
verses.40:10: and the side chambers of the gate were side chamber opposite side chamber, three on this side and three on that side, and one measure for the three, and one measure for the vestibules on this side and on that side.
verses.40:11: And he measured the width of the doorway of the gateway, ten cubits, and the breadth of the gateway, thirteen cubits.
verses.40:12: And a cubit drew inward in front of the side chambers on this side and on that side, and the side chamber was six cubits on this side and six cubits on that side.
verses.40:13: And he measured the gate from the wall of the side chamber to the wall of the side chamber, a width of twenty-five cubits; this gate faced the opposite gate.
verses.40:14: And the forecourt of the vestibule of the gate on the outside was twenty cubits, with side chambers of the gate all around.
verses.40:15: And from the forecourt of the gate on the outside to the forecourt of the vestibule of the gate on the inside was fifty cubits.
verses.40:16: And there were concealed windows upon the side chambers and upon the vestibules inside the gate of the court all around; and likewise for the vestibules there were windows all around on the inside, and upon the vestibule were palm trees on this side and on that side.
verses.40:17: And he brought me into the inner court, and behold, there were chambers and colonnades of the court all around, thirty chambers in the colonnades,
verses.40:18: and the porticoes were behind the gates; according to the length of the gates was the lower colonnade.
verses.40:19: And he measured the width of the court from the forecourt of the outer gate on the inside to the forecourt of the gate facing outward, one hundred cubits, of the gate facing toward the east. And he led me toward the north,
verses.40:20: and behold, a gate facing toward the north belonging to the outer court; and he measured it, both its length and its width,
verses.40:21: and the side chambers, three on this side and three on that side, and the posts and the vestibules and its palm trees. And it was according to the measurements of the gate facing toward the east: fifty cubits was its length, and twenty-five cubits was its breadth.
verses.40:22: And its windows and the vestibules and its palm trees were like the gate facing toward the east; and by seven steps they went up to it, and the vestibules were on the inside.
verses.40:23: And there was a gate for the inner court facing the gate of the north, in the same manner as the gate facing toward the east; and he measured the court from gate to gate, one hundred cubits.
verses.40:24: And he led me toward the south, and behold, a gate facing toward the south; and he measured it and the side chambers and the posts and the vestibules according to these measurements.
verses.40:25: And its windows and the vestibules all around were like the windows of the vestibule; fifty cubits was its length, and twenty-five cubits was its breadth.
verses.40:26: And it had seven steps and vestibules on the inside, and palm trees upon it, one on this side and one on that side upon the posts.
verses.40:27: And there was a gate opposite the gate of the inner court toward the south; and he measured the court from gate to gate, one hundred cubits in breadth toward the south.
verses.40:28: And he brought me into the inner court of the gate toward the south, and he measured the gate according to these measurements,
verses.40:29: and the side chambers and the posts and the vestibules according to these measurements, and there were windows for it and for the vestibule all around; fifty cubits was its length, and the breadth twenty-five cubits
verses.40:31: of the vestibule toward the outer court, and palm trees on the posts, and eight steps.
verses.40:32: And he brought me into the gate facing toward the east, and he measured it according to these measurements,
verses.40:33: and the side chambers and the posts and the vestibules according to these measurements, and there were windows for it and the vestibules all around; fifty cubits was its length, and its breadth twenty-five cubits.
verses.40:34: And the vestibules were toward the inner court, and palm trees were upon the posts on this side and on that side, and it had eight steps.
verses.40:35: And he brought me into the gate toward the north, and he measured according to these measurements,
verses.40:36: and the side chambers and the posts and the vestibules, and there were windows for it all around and for its vestibule; fifty cubits was its length, and its breadth twenty-five cubits;
verses.40:37: and the vestibules were toward the outer court, and palm trees were on the posts on this side and on that side, and it had eight steps.
verses.40:38: Its chambers and its doorways and its vestibules at the second gate had a drain,
verses.40:39: so that they might slay in it the offerings for sin and for ignorance.
verses.40:40: And behind the channel of the burnt offerings of the gate facing toward the north were two tables toward the east behind the second gate, and at the vestibule of the gate were two tables toward the east.
verses.40:41: Four on this side and four on that side behind the gate; upon them they shall slay the sacrifices, opposite the eight tables of the sacrifices.
verses.40:42: And four tables of the burnt offerings were of hewn stone, a cubit and a half in width, and two and a half cubits in length, and one cubit in height; upon them they shall place the instruments with which they slay the burnt offerings and the sacrifices there.
verses.40:43: And they shall have a hewn rim of one handbreadth all around on the inside, and over the tables above, coverings to shelter them from the rain and from the drought.
verses.40:44: And he brought me into the inner court, and behold, there were two halls in the inner court: one behind the gate facing toward the north, opening toward the south, and one behind the gate toward the south, facing toward the north.
verses.40:45: And he said to me, "This hall that faces toward the south is for the priests who keep the charge of the house;
verses.40:46: and the hall that faces toward the north is for the priests who keep the charge of the altar. These are the sons of Zadok, who draw near from Levi to the Lord to minister to Him."
verses.40:47: And he measured the court: a length of one hundred cubits and a breadth of one hundred cubits on its four sides; and the altar was opposite the house.
verses.40:48: And he brought me into the vestibule of the house. And he measured the post of the vestibule, five cubits in width on this side and five cubits on that side; and the breadth of the doorway was fourteen cubits, and the shoulders of the door of the vestibule were three cubits on this side and three cubits on that side.
verses.40:49: And the length of the vestibule was twenty cubits, and the breadth twelve cubits; and by ten steps they went up to it, and there were pillars by the vestibule, one on this side and one on that side.
verses.41:1: And he brought me into the temple, of which he measured the vestibule: six cubits in width on this side,
verses.41:2: and six cubits the breadth of the vestibule on that side; and the breadth of the gateway was ten cubits, and the side walls of the gateway were five cubits on this side and five cubits on that side. And he measured its length, forty cubits, and the breadth, twenty cubits.
verses.41:3: And he went into the inner court and measured the jamb of the doorway, two cubits; and the doorway, six cubits; and the side walls of the doorway, seven cubits on this side and seven cubits on that side.
verses.41:4: And he measured the length of the doors, forty cubits, and a breadth of twenty cubits before the face of the temple. And he said, "This is the Holy of Holies."
verses.41:5: And he measured the wall of the house, six cubits, and the breadth of the side chamber, four cubits all around,
verses.41:6: and the side chambers, side chamber upon side chamber, thirty, three times, twice; and there was a space in the wall of the house among the side chambers round about, for those who take hold to see, so that they might not touch the walls of the house at all.
verses.41:7: And the breadth of the upper side chamber was according to the addition from the wall, toward the upper level round about the house, so that it might be widened above, and so that from the lower chambers they might ascend to the upper chambers, and from the cornices to the third-story chambers,
verses.41:8: and the thrael of the house was a height round about; the space of the side chambers was equal to a reed of six cubits. The spaces
verses.41:9: and the breadth of the wall of the side chamber on the outside were five cubits, and the remaining spaces that were between the side chambers of the house
verses.41:10: and between the chambers were twenty cubits in breadth, encircling the house round about.
verses.41:11: And the doors of the chambers opened toward the remaining space of the one door toward the north; and the one door was toward the south, and the breadth of the light of the remaining space was five cubits in width all around.
verses.41:12: And the open-air structure in front of the remaining space toward the sea was seventy cubits; the width of the dividing wall was five cubits in breadth all around, and its length was ninety cubits.
verses.41:13: And he measured opposite the house a length of one hundred cubits, and the remaining spaces and the partitions and their walls were one hundred cubits in length,
verses.41:14: and the breadth before the face of the house and the remaining spaces opposite were one hundred cubits.
verses.41:15: And he measured the length of the partition in front of the remaining space of the parts behind that house, and the remaining spaces on this side and on that side were one hundred cubits in length. And the temple, and the corners, and the outer vestibule were paneled.
verses.41:16: And there were latticed windows, light openings round about for the three so as to look out; and the house and the adjoining parts were paneled with wood round about, and the floor, and from the floor to the windows, and the windows folded open in three parts for looking out.
verses.41:17: And even to near the inner part and even to the outer part, and upon the whole wall round about, on the inside and on the outside,
verses.41:18: were carved cherubim; and palm trees were between cherub and cherub. Each cherub had two faces,
verses.41:19: the face of a man toward the palm tree on this side and on that side, and the face of a lion toward the palm tree on this side and on that side; the house was carved all around;
verses.41:20: from the floor to the paneling, the cherubim and the palm trees were carved.
verses.41:21: And the sanctuary and the temple opened out foursquare; before the face of the holy places was a vision like the appearance
verses.41:22: of a wooden altar, its height three cubits, and its length two cubits, and its breadth two cubits; and it had horns, and its base and its walls were of wood. And he said to me, "This is the table that is before the presence." And the temple had two doorways,
verses.41:23: and the sanctuary had two doorways;
verses.41:24: for the two swinging doorways, there were two doors for the one, and two doors for the second door.
verses.41:25: And there was carved work upon them, and upon the doorways of the temple were cherubim, and palm trees according to the carved work of the holy places, and solid timbers before the face of the vestibule on the outside,
verses.41:26: and hidden windows. And he measured on this side and on that side, to the roofings of the vestibule, and the side chambers of the house were braced together.
verses.42:1: And he brought me into the inner court toward the east, opposite the gate toward the north; and he brought me in, and behold, five chambers adjoining the remaining space and adjoining the partition toward the north,
verses.42:2: extending one hundred cubits in length toward the north, and the width fifty,
verses.42:3: laid out in the same manner as the gates of the inner court, and in the same manner as the colonnades of the outer court, arranged in rows facing one another as threefold galleries.
verses.42:4: And opposite the chambers was a walkway ten cubits in width, extending one hundred cubits in length; and their doorways were toward the north,
verses.42:5: and the upper walkways were likewise. For the colonnade projected out from it, from the lower colonnade, and so did the space; thus there was a colonnade and a space, and thus two galleries.
verses.42:6: For they were threefold, and they did not have pillars like the pillars of the outer ones; therefore they projected from the lower and the middle ones from the ground.
verses.42:7: And there was a light outside, in the same manner as the chambers of the outer court that look opposite the chambers toward the north, fifty cubits in length.
verses.42:8: For the length of the chambers looking toward the outer court was fifty cubits, and these are the ones facing those; the whole was one hundred cubits.
verses.42:9: And the doors of these chambers of the entrance toward the east, to enter through them from the outer court,
verses.42:10: were opposite the light at the beginning of the walkway; and the parts toward the south were before the face of the south, before the face of the remaining space and before the face of the partition; and the chambers
verses.42:11: and the walkway in front of them were according to the measurements of the chambers toward the north, both according to their length and according to their breadth, and according to all their exits and according to all their turnings, and according to their lights and according to their doorways,
verses.42:12: of the chambers toward the south, and according to the doorways from the beginning of the walkway as toward the light of the space of a reed, and toward the east to enter through them.
verses.42:13: And he said to me, "The chambers toward the north and the chambers toward the south, which are before the spaces, these are the chambers of the sanctuary, in which the priests, the sons of Zadok, who draw near to the Lord, shall eat there the most holy things; and there they shall lay the most holy things, and the sacrifice, and the sin offerings, and the offerings for ignorance, because the place is holy.
verses.42:14: None shall enter there except the priests; they shall not go out from the sanctuary into the outer court, so that those who draw near may continually be holy; and they shall not touch their vestments in which they minister, because they are holy; and they shall put on other garments when they touch the people."
verses.42:15: And the measuring of the inner house was completed. And he brought me out by the way of the gate that faces toward the east, and he measured the pattern of the house round about in order.
verses.42:16: And he stood behind the gate that faces toward the east, and he measured five hundred with the measuring reed.
verses.42:17: And he turned toward the north and measured the side facing the north, five hundred cubits with the measuring reed.
verses.42:18: And he turned toward the sea and measured the side facing the sea, five hundred with the measuring reed.
verses.42:19: And he turned toward the south and measured opposite the south, five hundred with the measuring reed,
verses.42:20: the four sides of the same reed; and he laid it out and their surrounding wall round about, five hundred toward the east and five hundred cubits in breadth, to make a separation between the holy places and the outer wall that was in the arrangement of the house.
verses.43:1: And he brought me to the gate facing toward the east, and he led me out.
verses.43:2: And behold, the glory of the God of Israel was coming along the way toward the east, and the sound of the camp was like the sound of many redoubling their voices; and the earth shone forth like brightness from the glory round about.
verses.43:3: And the vision which I saw was like the vision which I saw when I went in to anoint the city, and the vision of the chariot which I saw was like the vision which I saw by the river Chebar; and I fell upon my face.
verses.43:4: And the glory of the Lord entered into the house by the way of the gate facing toward the east.
verses.43:5: And the Spirit took me up and brought me into the inner court; and behold, the house was full of the glory of the Lord.
verses.43:6: And I stood, and behold, a voice came out of the house, of One speaking to me, and the man was standing beside me,
verses.43:7: and He said to me, "Have you seen, son of man, the place of My throne and the place of the sole of My feet, in which My name shall dwell in the midst of the house of Israel forever? And the house of Israel shall no longer profane My holy name, they and their rulers, by their harlotry and by the murders of the rulers in their midst,
verses.43:8: when they set My doorway by their doorways and My doorposts beside their doorposts; and they made My wall as adjoining between Me and them, and they profaned My holy name by their iniquities which they committed; and I destroyed them in My wrath and in slaughter.
verses.43:9: And now let them cast away their harlotry and the murders of their rulers from Me, and I will dwell in their midst forever.
verses.43:10: And you, son of man, show the house to the house of Israel—and they shall cease from their sins—both its appearance and its arrangement,
verses.43:11: and they shall receive their punishment for all that they have done. And you shall draw out the house and its exits and its foundation; and all its ordinances and all its laws you shall make known to them and write down before them, and they shall keep all My statutes and all My ordinances and do them.
verses.43:12: And the plan of the house upon the top of the mountain—all its borders round about are holy of holies."
verses.43:13: And these are the measurements of the altar by the cubit of a cubit and a handbreadth: a recess of a cubit in depth, and a cubit in breadth, and a border upon its rim round about of a span. And this is the height of the altar:
verses.43:14: from the depth of the beginning of its hollow to this great propitiatory beneath is two cubits, and the breadth is a cubit. And from the small propitiatory to the great propitiatory is four cubits, and the breadth is a cubit.
verses.43:15: And the ariel is four cubits, and from the ariel and above the horns is a cubit.
verses.43:16: And the ariel is twelve cubits in length by twelve cubits, square upon its four sides.
verses.43:17: And the propitiatory is fourteen cubits in length by fourteen cubits in breadth on its four sides; and its border round about, encircling it, is half a cubit, and its circuit is a cubit round about; and its steps face toward the east.
verses.43:18: And He said to me, "Son of man, thus says the Lord God of Israel: These are the ordinances of the altar on the day it is made, to offer burnt offerings upon it and to pour out blood against it.
verses.43:19: And you shall give to the priests, the Levites, who are of the seed of Zadok, who draw near to Me, says the Lord God, to minister to Me, a young bull from the herd for a sin offering.
verses.43:20: And they shall take of its blood and put it upon the four horns of the altar, and upon the four corners of the propitiatory, and upon the base round about; and they shall make atonement for it.
verses.43:21: And they shall take the young bull of the sin offering, and it shall be burned in the set-apart place of the house, outside the sanctuary.
verses.43:22: And on the second day they shall take two unblemished kids of the goats for a sin offering, and they shall make atonement for the altar, just as they made atonement with the young bull.
verses.43:23: And after you have finished the atonement, they shall offer an unblemished young bull from the herd and an unblemished ram from the flock,
verses.43:24: and you shall present them before the Lord; and the priests shall cast salt upon them and offer them up as burnt offerings to the Lord.
verses.43:25: For seven days you shall prepare a young goat for a sin offering every day; also a young bull from the herd and a ram from the flock, without blemish, they shall prepare
verses.43:26: for seven days; and they shall make atonement for the altar and cleanse it, and they shall fill their hands.
verses.43:27: And it shall be from the eighth day and onward, the priests shall offer upon the altar your burnt offerings and your offerings of salvation; and I will accept you, says the Lord."
verses.44:1: And he brought me back by the way of the outer gate of the sanctuary facing toward the east, and it was shut.
verses.44:2: And the Lord said to me, "This gate shall be shut; it shall not be opened, and no one shall pass through it, because the Lord, the God of Israel, shall enter through it, and it shall be shut.
verses.44:3: For the ruler—he shall sit in it to eat bread before the Lord; he shall enter by the way of the vestibule of the gate, and by its way he shall go out."
verses.44:4: And he brought me by the way of the gate toward the north, opposite the house; and I looked, and behold, the house of the Lord was full of glory, and I fell upon my face.
verses.44:5: And the Lord said to me, "Son of man, set it in your heart, and see with your eyes, and hear with your ears all that I speak with you concerning all the ordinances of the house of the Lord and all its laws; and you shall set your heart upon the entrance of the house, with all its exits in all the holy places.
verses.44:6: And you shall say to the rebellious house, to the house of Israel, 'Thus says the Lord God: Let it be enough for you from all your iniquities, O house of Israel,
verses.44:7: that you brought in foreigners, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, to be in My sanctuary; and they profaned it when you offered bread, flesh, and blood, and you transgressed My covenant in all your iniquities,
verses.44:8: and you ordained the keeping of the charges in My sanctuary.
verses.44:9: Therefore thus says the Lord God: No foreigner, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, shall enter into My sanctuary, of all the foreigners who are in the midst of the house of Israel,
verses.44:10: except the Levites who broke away from Me when Israel went astray from Me after their own devices; and they shall bear their iniquity,
verses.44:11: and they shall be in My sanctuary ministering as gatekeepers at the gates of the house, and ministering to the house; they shall slay the burnt offerings and the sacrifices for the people, and they shall stand before the people to minister to them.
verses.44:12: Because they ministered to them before their idols, and it became to the house of Israel a punishment of iniquity, therefore I have lifted up My hand against them, says the Lord God,
verses.44:13: and they shall not draw near to Me to serve as priests to Me, nor approach the holy things of the sons of Israel, nor My holy of holies; and they shall bear their dishonor in the straying by which they went astray.
verses.44:14: And they shall bring them down to keep the charges of the house, for all its work and for all that they shall do.
verses.44:15: The priests, the Levites, the sons of Zadok, who kept the charges of My sanctuary when the house of Israel went astray from Me—these shall approach Me to minister to Me, and they shall stand before My face to offer to Me sacrifice, fat and blood, says the Lord God.
verses.44:16: These shall enter into My sanctuary, and these shall come near to My table to minister to Me, and they shall keep My charges.
verses.44:17: And it shall be, when they enter the gates of the inner court, they shall put on linen garments; and they shall not put on woolen garments while they minister from the gate of the inner court.
verses.44:18: And they shall have linen turbans upon their heads, and they shall have linen breeches upon their loins, and they shall not gird themselves tightly.
verses.44:19: And when they go out into the outer court to the people, they shall take off their garments in which they minister, and they shall lay them in the chambers of the sanctuary, and they shall put on other garments; and they shall not sanctify the people with their garments.
verses.44:20: And they shall not shave their heads, nor strip bare their hair; they shall surely cover their heads.
verses.44:21: And no priest shall drink wine when they enter into the inner court.
verses.44:22: And they shall not take a widow or a divorced woman for themselves as a wife, but only a virgin of the seed of Israel; yet if there is a widow of a priest, they may take her.
verses.44:23: And they shall teach My people the difference between the holy and the profane, and make known to them the difference between the clean and the unclean;
verses.44:24: and in a judgment of blood they shall stand to decide; they shall uphold My statutes and judge My judgments, and they shall keep My laws and My ordinances in all My feasts, and they shall sanctify My Sabbaths.
verses.44:25: And they shall not go in to a dead person to be defiled; except for father and mother, and for son and for daughter, and for brother, and for his sister who has had no husband, he may be defiled.
verses.44:26: And after he is cleansed, he shall count off seven days for himself;
verses.44:27: and on whatever day they enter into the inner court to minister in the holy place, they shall offer a propitiation, says the Lord God.
verses.44:28: And it shall be to them for an inheritance: I am their inheritance; and no possession shall be given to them among the sons of Israel, for I am their possession.
verses.44:29: And the sacrifices and the sin offerings and the offerings for ignorance, these they shall eat; and every devoted thing in Israel shall be theirs.
verses.44:30: The firstfruits of all things, and the firstborn of all things, and all the offerings set apart from all your firstfruits shall belong to the priests. And your first produce you shall give to the priest, to place your blessings upon your houses.
verses.44:31: And the priests shall not eat anything that died of itself or was torn by wild beasts, whether of birds or of cattle.'"
verses.45:1: And when you measure out the land for an inheritance, you shall set apart a firstfruits offering to the Lord, a holy portion from the land, twenty-five thousand in length and twenty thousand in width; it shall be holy throughout all its borders all around.
verses.45:2: And from this there shall be a sanctuary, five hundred by five hundred, square all around, and fifty cubits for an open space around it.
verses.45:3: And from this measurement you shall measure a length of twenty-five thousand and a width of twenty thousand, and in it shall be the Holy of Holies.
verses.45:4: It shall be from the land for the priests who minister in the holy place, and it shall be for those who draw near to minister to the Lord; and it shall be a place for them for houses set apart for their sanctuary,
verses.45:5: twenty-five thousand in length and twenty thousand in width; and for the Levites who minister to the house, for them as a possession, cities to dwell in.
verses.45:6: And you shall give as the possession of the city five thousand in width and twenty-five thousand in length, corresponding to the firstfruits offering of the holy portions; they shall belong to the whole house of Israel.
verses.45:7: And for the ruler, on this side and on that side bordering the firstfruits offerings of the holy portions and the possession of the city, facing the firstfruits offerings of the holy portions and facing the possession of the city, on the side toward the sea and from the side toward the sea eastward; and the length shall be like one of the portions, from the borders toward the sea, and the length to the borders toward the east of the land.
verses.45:8: And it shall be to him for a possession in Israel, and the rulers of Israel shall no longer oppress My people; and the house of Israel shall inherit the land according to their tribes.
verses.45:9: Thus says the Lord God: "Let it be enough for you, O rulers of Israel! Put away injustice and misery, and execute judgment and righteousness; remove oppression from My people," says the Lord God.
verses.45:10: "You shall have a just balance, a just measure, and a just choenix of the measure,
verses.45:11: and the choenix likewise shall be one standard for receiving: the tenth of the gomor shall be a choenix, and the tenth of the gomor; its equal measure shall be according to the gomor.
verses.45:12: And the weights shall be twenty obols; five shekels, five, and ten shekels, and fifty shekels shall be the mina for you.
verses.45:13: And this is the firstfruits offering that you shall set apart: a sixth of a measure from a gomor of wheat, and a sixth of that ephah from a kor of barley.
verses.45:14: And the ordinance of oil: a kotyle of oil from ten kotyles, for ten kotyles are a gomor.
verses.45:15: And one sheep from the flock out of ten, a tribute from all the families of Israel, for sacrifices and for burnt offerings and for offerings of deliverance, to make atonement for you," says the Lord God.
verses.45:16: And all the people shall give this firstfruits offering to the ruler of Israel.
verses.45:17: And through the ruler shall be the burnt offerings and the sacrifices and the drink offerings at the feasts, and at the new moons, and on the Sabbaths, and at all the feasts of the house of Israel; he himself shall offer the sin offerings and the sacrifice and the burnt offerings and the offerings of deliverance, to make atonement for the house of Israel.
verses.45:18: Thus says the Lord God: "In the first month, on the first day of the month, you shall take a young bull without blemish from the herd to make atonement for the sanctuary.
verses.45:19: And the priest shall take some of the blood of the atonement offering and put it on the doorposts of the house, and on the four corners of the temple, and on the altar, and on the doorposts of the gate of the inner court.
verses.45:20: And so you shall do in the seventh month, on the first day of the month, a portion from each one, and you shall make atonement for the house.
verses.45:21: And in the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, you shall have the Passover, a feast; for seven days you shall eat unleavened bread.
verses.45:22: And on that day the ruler shall offer for himself and for the house and for all the people of the land a young bull for a sin offering.
verses.45:23: And during the seven days of the feast he shall offer burnt offerings to the Lord: seven young bulls and seven rams without blemish daily for the seven days, and a kid of the goats daily for a sin offering, and a sacrifice.
verses.45:24: And you shall prepare a cake for each young bull and a cake for each ram, and a hin of oil for each cake.
verses.45:25: And in the seventh month, on the fifteenth day of the month, at the feast, you shall do the same for seven days, according to the sin offerings, and according to the burnt offerings, and according to the grain offering, and according to the oil."
verses.46:1: Thus says the Lord God: "The gate of the inner court that faces toward the east shall be shut during the six working days; on the Sabbath day it shall be opened, and on the day of the new moon it shall be opened.
verses.46:2: And the ruler shall enter by the way of the porch of the inner gate and shall stand at the entrance of the gate, and the priests shall offer his burnt offerings and his offerings of deliverance.
verses.46:3: And he shall worship at the threshold of the gate and go out, and the gate shall not be shut until evening; and the people of the land shall worship at the entrance of that gate both on the Sabbaths and at the new moons before the Lord.
verses.46:4: And the burnt offerings that the ruler shall bring to the Lord on the Sabbath day shall be six lambs without blemish and a ram without blemish,
verses.46:5: and a grain offering, a cake for the ram, and for the lambs a sacrifice as a gift of his hand, and a hin of oil for each cake.
verses.46:6: And on the day of the new moon, a young bull without blemish and six lambs, and there shall be a ram without blemish;
verses.46:7: and a cake for the ram and a cake for the young bull shall be the grain offering, and for the lambs according as his hand is able to afford, and a hin of oil for each cake.
verses.46:8: And when the ruler enters, he shall enter by the way of the porch of the gate, and he shall go out by the way of the gate.
verses.46:9: And when the people of the land enter before the Lord at the feasts, the one who enters by the way of the gate facing north to worship shall go out by the way of the gate toward the south, and the one who enters by the way of the gate toward the south shall go out by the way of the gate toward the north; he shall not return by the gate through which he has entered, but shall go out straight opposite it.
verses.46:10: And the ruler shall be in their midst; when they enter, he shall enter with them, and when they go out, he shall go out.
verses.46:11: And at the feasts and at the solemn assemblies, the grain offering shall be a cake for each young bull and a cake for each ram, and for the lambs according as his hand is able to afford, and a hin of oil for each cake.
verses.46:12: And if the ruler offers a freewill offering, a burnt offering of deliverance to the Lord, he shall open for himself the gate facing east, and he shall offer his burnt offering and his offerings of deliverance just as he does on the Sabbath day; and he shall go out, and he shall shut the doors after he has gone out.
verses.46:13: And he shall offer a lamb of the first year without blemish for a burnt offering daily to the Lord; in the morning he shall offer it.
verses.46:14: And he shall prepare a grain offering with it in the morning, a sixth of a measure, and a third of a hin of oil to mingle with the fine flour—a grain offering to the Lord, a perpetual ordinance.
verses.46:15: You shall offer the lamb, and the grain offering and the oil you shall offer in the morning, as a perpetual burnt offering."
verses.46:16: Thus says the Lord God: "If the ruler gives a gift to one of his sons from his inheritance, this shall belong to his sons as a possession by inheritance.
verses.46:17: But if he gives a gift to one of his servants, then it shall be his until the year of release, and he shall return it to the ruler; only the inheritance of his sons shall belong to them.
verses.46:18: And the ruler shall by no means take from the inheritance of the people to oppress them; from his own possession he shall give an inheritance to his sons, so that My people may not be scattered, each one from his possession."
verses.46:19: Then he brought me into the entrance behind the gate, into the chamber of the holy things of the priests facing north; and behold, there was a place set apart there.
verses.46:20: And he said to me, "This is the place where the priests shall boil the offerings for ignorance and the sin offerings, and where they shall bake the grain offering, so as not to bring them out at all into the outer court to sanctify the people."
verses.46:21: Then he brought me out into the outer court and led me around to the four parts of the court; and behold, there was a court at the sides of the court;
verses.46:22: at each side a court, a court at all four, and a small court belonging to the court, forty cubits in length and thirty cubits in width, one measure for the four.
verses.46:23: And there were chambers all around in them, all around the four; and kitchens were made underneath the chambers all around.
verses.46:24: And he said to me, "These are the houses of the cooks, where those who minister to the house shall boil the sacrifices of the people."
verses.47:1: Then he brought me to the entrance of the house; and behold, water was flowing out from underneath the open court toward the east, for the front of the house faced east; and the water was coming down from the right side, from the south, to the altar.
verses.47:2: And he brought me out by the way of the north gate, and led me around by the outside way to the gate of the court that faces east; and behold, the water was rushing down from the right side,
verses.47:3: just as a man goes out opposite. And a measure was in his hand; and he measured one thousand with the measure, and he passed through in the water—water of release;
verses.47:4: and he measured one thousand, and he passed through in the water—water up to the thighs; and he measured one thousand, and he passed through water up to the loins.
verses.47:5: And he measured one thousand, and he could not pass through, for it was surging violently like a torrent that they shall not cross.
verses.47:6: And he said to me, "Have you seen this, son of man?" And he led me to the bank of the river
verses.47:7: upon my return; and behold, along the bank of the river were very many trees on this side and on that side.
verses.47:8: And he said to me, "This water goes out toward Galilee to the east, and went down into Arabia, and came to the sea, to the water of the outlet, and it shall heal the waters;
verses.47:9: and it shall be that every living soul of the creatures that swarm, wherever the river comes there, shall live; and there shall be very many fish there, because this water has come there, and it shall heal and live; everything to which the river comes there shall live.
verses.47:10: And fishermen shall stand there from En Gedi to En Eglaim; it shall be a drying place for dragnets, it shall be by itself; and its fish shall be like the fish of the Great Sea, a very great multitude.
verses.47:11: And at its outlet and at its backwater and at its overflow they shall not be healed; they are given over to salt.
verses.47:12: And along the river, upon its bank on this side and on that side, every tree for food shall grow up; nothing upon it shall grow old, nor shall its fruit fail; in its newness it shall bear firstfruits, because these waters of theirs flow out from the sanctuary; and their fruit shall be for food, and their growth for healing."
verses.47:13: Thus says the Lord God: "These are the borders of the land that you shall inherit: for the twelve tribes of the sons of Israel, an addition of a measuring line.
verses.47:14: And you shall inherit it, each one just like his brother, the land concerning which I lifted up My hand to give it to their fathers; and this land shall fall to you as an inheritance.
verses.47:15: And these are the borders of the land on the north side: from the Great Sea that goes down and divides around, by the entrance of Hema, Seldamma,
verses.47:16: Abthera, Sebram, Heliam, between the borders of Damascus and between the borders of Hamath, the court of Saunan, which are above the borders of Hauranitis.
verses.47:17: These are the borders from the sea: from the court of Enan, the borders of Damascus, and the regions to the north.
verses.47:18: And the regions to the east: between Loranitis and Damascus, and between Gileaditis and the land of Israel, the Jordan forms the border to the sea that is east of Phoenicon; these are the regions to the east.
verses.47:19: And the regions to the south and southwest: from Teman and Phoenicon to the water of Marimoth Kadem, extending along to the Great Sea;
verses.47:20: this part is south and southwest. This part the Great Sea borders, as far as opposite the entrance of Hamath, even to its entrance; these are the regions toward the sea of Hamath.
verses.47:21: And you shall divide this land for them, for the tribes of Israel.
verses.47:22: You shall cast it by lot for yourselves and for the proselytes who sojourn in your midst, who have fathered sons in your midst, and they shall be to you as native-born among the sons of Israel; with you they shall eat in an inheritance in the midst of the tribes of Israel,
verses.47:23: and they shall be in the tribe of the proselytes, among the proselytes who are with them; there you shall give an inheritance to them," says the Lord God.
verses.48:1: And these are the names of the tribes from the northern extremity, along the side of the descent of that which divides, to the entrance of Hamath, the court of Ailam, the border of Damascus toward the north beside the side of the court of Hamath; and theirs shall be the parts toward the east as far as the sea: Dan, one portion.
verses.48:2: And from the borders of Dan, the side toward the east as far as the side toward the sea: Asher, one portion.
verses.48:3: And from the borders of Asher, from the side toward the east as far as the side toward the sea: Naphtali, one portion.
verses.48:4: And from the borders of Naphtali, from the east as far as the side toward the sea: Manasseh, one portion.
verses.48:5: And from the borders of Manasseh, from the side toward the east as far as the side toward the sea: Ephraim, one portion.
verses.48:6: And from the borders of Ephraim, from the side toward the east as far as the side toward the sea: Reuben, one portion.
verses.48:7: And from the borders of Reuben, from the side toward the east as far as the side toward the sea: Judah, one portion.
verses.48:8: And from the borders of Judah, from the side toward the east it shall remain: the firstfruits of the setting apart shall be twenty-five thousand in width, and in length like one of the portions from the side toward the east even to the side toward the sea; and the sanctuary shall be in their midst.
verses.48:9: The firstfruits offering which they shall set apart to the Lord shall be twenty-five thousand in length, and twenty-five thousand in width.
verses.48:10: Out of these shall be the firstfruits of the holy things for the priests: toward the north, twenty-five thousand; and toward the sea, ten thousand; and toward the south, twenty-five thousand; and the mountain of the holy things shall be in its midst.
verses.48:11: For the sanctified priests, the sons of Zadok, who keep the charges of the house, who did not go astray in the straying of the sons of Israel, just as the Levites went astray.
verses.48:12: And theirs shall be the firstfruits offering given from the firstfruits of the land, a most holy portion, from the borders of the Levites.
verses.48:13: And for the Levites, the parts adjoining the borders of the priests shall be twenty-five thousand in length, and ten thousand in width; the entire length shall be twenty-five thousand, and the width twenty thousand.
verses.48:14: Nothing of it shall be sold, nor shall it be measured out, nor shall the first produce of the land be taken away, for it is holy to the Lord.
verses.48:15: And the five thousand remaining in breadth alongside the twenty-five thousand shall be an outer rampart for the city, for dwelling and for its open space; and the city shall be in its midst.
verses.48:16: And these shall be its measurements: on the side toward the north, four thousand five hundred; and on the side toward the south, four thousand five hundred; and on the side toward the east, four thousand five hundred; and on the side toward the sea, four thousand five hundred.
verses.48:17: And the city shall have open space: toward the north, two hundred fifty; and toward the south, two hundred fifty; and toward the east, two hundred fifty; and toward the sea, two hundred fifty.
verses.48:18: And the remainder of the length adjoining the firstfruits of the holy things shall be ten thousand toward the east, and ten thousand toward the sea; and they shall be the firstfruits of the sanctuary, and its produce shall be for bread for those who work the city.
verses.48:19: And those who work the city shall work it from all the tribes of Israel.
verses.48:20: The entire firstfruits offering shall be twenty-five thousand by twenty-five thousand; foursquare you shall set apart from it the first part of the sanctuary, from the possession of the city.
verses.48:21: And the remainder shall be for the ruler, on this side and on that side of the firstfruits of the sanctuary and toward the possession of the city, extending twenty-five thousand in length as far as the borders toward the east, and toward the sea extending twenty-five thousand as far as the borders toward the sea, adjoining the portions of the ruler; and the firstfruits of the holy things and the sanctuary of the house shall be in its midst.
verses.48:22: And from the Levites, from the possession of the city, it shall be in the midst of the rulers, between the borders of Judah and between the borders of Benjamin; it shall belong to the rulers.
verses.48:23: And as for the rest of the tribes: from the side toward the east as far as the side toward the sea, Benjamin, one portion.
verses.48:24: And from the borders of Benjamin, from the side toward the east as far as the side toward the sea: Simeon, one portion.
verses.48:25: And from the borders of Simeon, from the side toward the east as far as the side toward the sea: Issachar, one portion.
verses.48:26: And from the borders of Issachar, from the side toward the east as far as the side toward the sea: Zebulun, one portion.
verses.48:27: And from the borders of Zebulun, from the side toward the east as far as the side toward the sea: Gad, one portion.
verses.48:28: And from the borders of Gad as far as the side toward the southwest, its borders shall be from Teman and the water of Barimoth Kadesh, of the inheritance, as far as the Great Sea.
verses.48:29: This is the land which you shall cast by lot for the tribes of Israel, and these are their divisions, says the Lord God.
verses.48:30: And these are the exits of the city on the side toward the north: four thousand five hundred by measure.
verses.48:31: And the gates of the city shall be after the names of the tribes of Israel: three gates toward the north—one gate of Reuben, and one gate of Judah, and one gate of Levi.
verses.48:32: And on the side toward the east, four thousand five hundred; and three gates—one gate of Joseph, and one gate of Benjamin, and one gate of Dan.
verses.48:33: And on the side toward the south, four thousand five hundred by measure; and three gates—one gate of Simeon, and one gate of Issachar, and one gate of Zebulun.
verses.48:34: And on the side toward the sea, four thousand five hundred by measure; and three gates—one gate of Gad, and one gate of Asher, and one gate of Naphtali.
verses.48:35: The circumference shall be eighteen thousand. And the name of the city, from whatever day it comes into being, shall be its name.

notes.1:2: Greek reads Ioakeim (Jehoiakim), a form the Septuagint often uses for both Jehoiakim and Jehoiachin; the Hebrew MT reads Jehoiachin.
notes.1:7: The Septuagint uniquely describes the living creatures as having winged feet, sparks like flashing bronze, and light wings, differing markedly from the Hebrew MT.
notes.1:15: Verse 14 of the Hebrew MT is absent from the Septuagint text.
notes.1:16: Greek tharseis transliterates the Hebrew gemstone name Tarshish, traditionally identified as beryl or chrysolite.
notes.1:20: The Septuagint reads "the cloud" and "a spirit of life," whereas the Hebrew MT reads "the spirit" and "the spirit of the living creature."
notes.2:1: The Septuagint opens chapter 2 with the sentence that closes 1:28 in the Hebrew MT.
notes.2:5: Greek ptoethosin ("be dismayed") differs from the Hebrew MT ("refuse" or "forbear").
notes.2:6: Where the Hebrew MT mentions briers and thorns, the Septuagint reads verbs of fierce hostility ("rage furiously and rise up against you").
notes.3:2: The Septuagint reads third-person "He opened" rather than the Hebrew MT's first-person "I opened."
notes.3:7: The Septuagint renders "contentious" here and "contention" in 3:8 where the Hebrew MT speaks of a hard "forehead."
notes.3:9: Greek dia pantos ("continually") reflects a reading of the Hebrew consonantal text as "always" rather than "adamant" or "emery."
notes.3:15: Greek meteoros ("aloft" or "suspended in midair") interprets the Hebrew expression that the MT treats as the place name Tel-abib.
notes.4:4: The Septuagint specifies "one hundred and fifty" days here and "one hundred and ninety" days in verses 5 and 9, whereas the Masoretic Text gives no number in verse 4 and reads "three hundred and ninety" days in verses 5 and 9.
notes.4:5: The Greek reads "their two iniquities" (tas dyo adikias auton), reflecting a reading of the Hebrew consonantal text as "two" rather than "years of."
notes.4:14: The Greek kreas heolon ("stale meat" or "meat kept overnight") renders the Hebrew term for tainted sacrificial flesh.
notes.5:2: Both here and in verse 12 the Septuagint divides the hair and the city's population into four fourths (burning two fourths here, corresponding to death and famine in verse 12), whereas the Masoretic Text divides them into thirds.
notes.5:6: The Greek reads "you shall declare" (ereis) to "the lawless one" (te anomo), diverging from the Masoretic Text's "she has rebelled against My ordinances with wickedness."
notes.5:15: The rare Greek pair stenakte kai delaiste ("an object of groaning and wretchedness") portrays Jerusalem as both lamented and pitiable among the surrounding nations.
notes.6:4: The Greek temene ("sacred precincts" or "shrines") translates the Hebrew term for incense altars, here and in verse 6.
notes.6:9: The Septuagint reads "I have sworn" (omomoka) against their unfaithful heart and "they shall beat their faces," diverging from the Masoretic Text's "I was crushed" and "they will loathe themselves."
notes.6:11: The Greek exclamation Euge, euge ("Aha! Aha!" or "Well done! Well done!") conveys sharp irony and derision over Israel's abominations.
notes.6:14: "Deblatha" preserves the Septuagint place-name Deblatha, corresponding to "Diblathah" (often identified with Riblah in Syria) in the Masoretic Text.
notes.7:4: The Greek reads "not with tumults, nor with pangs" and follows a distinct order and wording across verses 3–9 compared to the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.7:13: Literally "in the eye of his life" (en ophthalmō zōēs autou), a distinctive Septuagint rendering reflecting a different reading of the Hebrew consonant text ("in his iniquity").
notes.7:22: "My oversight" (tēn episkopēn mou) translates the Greek term for visitation or charge, where the Hebrew tradition refers to God's treasured or secret place; likewise verse 23 reads "confusion" (phyrmon) and "full of peoples" (plērēs laōn).
notes.7:25: "Atonement" (exilasmos) is a notable Septuagint reading where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "anguish" or "destruction."
notes.8:1: The Greek dates this vision to the "fifth month" (MT: sixth month), and in verse 2 describes "a likeness of a man" (MT: "fire").
notes.8:3: "The pillar of the one who acquires" (hē stēlē tou ktōmenou) reflects the Greek translator's rendering of the Hebrew root as "acquire" rather than "jealousy."
notes.8:11: The Greek gives the name "Jeconiah" (Iechonias), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "Jaazaniah."
notes.8:16: The Greek numbers the men as "about twenty" (MT: twenty-five), transliterates the architectural term for porches as plural ailam, and in verse 17 renders the closing gesture as "those who mock" (myktērizontes, literally turning up the nose).
notes.9:2: "A belt of sapphire" (zōnē sappheirou) is a distinctive Septuagint rendering where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "a scribe's inkhorn."
notes.9:3: "The open court" (to aithrion) renders the Greek architectural term for an open atrium or courtyard, corresponding to "the threshold" in the Hebrew tradition.
notes.9:9: "Filled with many peoples" (laōn pollōn) preserves a distinctive Septuagint reading shared with 7:23, where the Hebrew tradition reads "blood."
notes.10:4: Greek aithrion denotes an open court or atrium of the temple, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "threshold."
notes.10:5: Greek theou Saddai preserves the transliterated Hebrew divine title Shaddai ("the Almighty").
notes.10:13: Greek Gelgel transliterates Hebrew galgal ("whirling wheel"); verse 14 of the Hebrew text (listing the four faces) is absent from the Greek text.
notes.10:21: The Greek text reads "eight wings" for each cherub, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "four wings."
notes.11:1: The Greek text names "Jechoniah the son of Ezer," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "Jaazaniah the son of Azzur."
notes.11:3: The Greek renders the leaders' boast as a rhetorical question ("Have not the houses been built recently?"), differing from the Hebrew ("The time is not near to build houses").
notes.11:10: The Greek reads "on the mountains of Israel" rather than "at the border of Israel" in the Hebrew text; verses 11–12 of the Hebrew text are absent from the Greek.
notes.11:15: The Greek reads "the men of your captivity" and "has come to an end," differing from the Hebrew ("your kinsmen" and "all of it").
notes.11:24: The Greek verb is first-person ("I went up from the vision"), whereas the Hebrew describes the vision ascending from the prophet.
notes.12:6: The Greek uses the passive "you shall be lifted up upon shoulders" and "concealed" (also in verses 7 and 12), where the Hebrew describes bearing baggage on the shoulder in the dark.
notes.12:10: Greek kyrios Kyrios doubles the divine title ("the Lord, the Lord"), and reads "The ruler and the leader" where the Hebrew reads "This burden [concerns] the prince."
notes.12:19: The Greek reads "in ungodliness" (asebeia) where the Hebrew reads "because of the violence."
notes.13:5: The Greek Septuagint reads "in a firm place," "gathered flocks," and "those who say, 'In the day of the Lord,'" differing notably from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's imagery of repairing a breach in a wall for battle.
notes.13:10: Greek "it shall fall" (peseitai) reflects the Septuagint's rendering of the Hebrew word for untempered mortar or whitewash as a form of the verb "to fall," a refrain repeated in verses 11, 14, and 15.
notes.13:14: The Greek reads "with reproofs" (met' elenchon), where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "in the midst of it."
notes.13:20: The doubled Greek divine title kyrios Kyrios is rendered literally as "the Lord, the Lord" (also in 14:6), and the Greek "into dispersion" (eis diaskorpismon) differs from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "like birds."
notes.14:3: Here and in verses 4-7, the Greek translates the Hebrew expressions for idols and stumbling blocks as "thoughts" or "devisings" (dianoemata, enthymemata) and "punishment" (kolasin).
notes.14:5: The Greek uses a third-person singular verb (plagiase, "may turn aside"), referring grammatically to "his mind" from verse 4 (or to the prophet/man), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "to seize."
notes.14:19: Greek thanatos ("death") is the Septuagint's standard rendering for deadly pestilence in this oracle (also in verse 21).
notes.14:22: The Greek has an active participle/verb ("who bring out") and omits the consolation clause found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text in verses 22-23.
notes.15:4: The Greek reads "its yearly pruning" (ten kat' eniauton katharsin), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text refers to "both of its ends."
notes.15:7: The Greek has future tense "they shall come out" and third-person plural "they shall know," where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads past tense and second-person plural.
notes.16:4: The Septuagint reads "you did not bind your breasts" (οὐκ ἔδησας τοὺς μαστούς σου) rather than the Masoretic Text's "your navel cord was not cut."
notes.16:7: The Septuagint reads "cities of cities" (πόλεις πόλεων), contrasting with the Masoretic Text's "finest ornaments."
notes.16:8: The Greek phrase "a time of those who lodge" (καιρὸς καταλυόντων) diverges from the Masoretic Text's "time for love."
notes.16:30: The Septuagint reads "How shall I deal with your daughter" and "committed harlotry threefold among your daughters," diverging sharply from the Masoretic Text's "How degenerate is your heart... the deeds of a brazen harlot."
notes.16:31: Unlike the Masoretic Text ("you were not like a harlot, because you scorned payment"), the Septuagint states that Jerusalem "became like a harlot gathering wages," followed in verse 32 by taking wages from her husband and paying them to those who committed harlotry with her.
notes.16:36: The Septuagint translates the Hebrew literally as "your bronze" (τὸν χαλκόν σου) and renders the term for idols as "devices" (ἐνθυμήματα).
notes.16:53: The Septuagint renders the Hebrew idiom for restoring fortunes literally as "turn back their turnings" (ἀποστρέψω τὰς ἀποστροφὰς αὐτῶν).
notes.16:57: The Septuagint reads "Syria" (Συρίας, reflecting Hebrew Aram) where many Masoretic manuscripts read "Edom," and translates "Philistines" literally as "foreigners" (ἀλλοφύλων).
notes.16:61: The Septuagint reads "for building up" (εἰς οἰκοδομήν), reading the Hebrew consonants as "to build" rather than the Masoretic Text's "as daughters."
notes.17:3: The Greek reads "full of talons" and "who has the design," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "full of plumage" and "of variegated colors."
notes.17:12: The Greek frames the Babylonian king's arrival prospectively ("When the king of Babylon comes... he shall take"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text speaks in the past tense.
notes.17:18: The Greek reads the first-person verb "I have given his hand," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text has the third-person "he gave his hand"; similarly, verse 16 reads "My curse" and "My covenant" in the Greek.
notes.17:23: The Greek reads "I will suspend it" (reflecting a Hebrew root meaning "to hang" rather than "lofty") and concludes with "its branches shall be restored," where the Hebrew reads "in the shadow of its branches they shall dwell."
notes.18:6: The Greek renders the Hebrew term for idols with a word meaning "devices" or "imaginations" (also in verse 15), highlighting inward idolatrous schemes, whereas verse 12 uses the standard word for "idols."
notes.18:11: The Greek reads "he did not walk in the way of his righteous father," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "though he himself did none of these things."
notes.18:30: The Greek reads "a punishment of iniquity," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "a stumbling block of iniquity."
notes.18:32: The Greek ends the chapter with "says the Lord," without the closing call "Therefore turn and live" found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.19:2: The Greek reads "A lion cub" and "she came into being," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "A lioness" and "she lay down."
notes.19:4: The Greek renders the Hebrew word for "pit" as "destruction" (also in verse 8), reflecting the related Hebrew root meaning "to destroy."
notes.19:7: The Greek reads "he fed in his boldness," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "he knew their widows" (or "their citadels").
notes.19:10: The Greek reads "like a vine and like a blossom on a pomegranate tree," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "like a vine in your blood" (or "in your likeness").
notes.20:1: The Greek text specifies the seventh year and the fifteenth of the month without naming the fifth month, whereas the Masoretic Text reads the fifth month and the tenth day.
notes.20:4: The Greek uses a first-person verb continuing the oath formula of verse 3 (literally, "if I will avenge them with vengeance"), rather than a second-person question directed to the prophet.
notes.20:6: The Greek reads "a honeycomb" (kerion) rather than "glory" or "beauty," echoing "milk and honey" (repeated in verse 15).
notes.20:26: The Greek uses the future tense ("I will defile them"), reads "when I pass through all that opens the womb," and omits the closing recognition formula found in the Masoretic Text.
notes.20:29: "Abana" is the Greek transliteration of the Hebrew term for "the high place" (ha-bamah), preserved here as a proper name in keeping with the Greek text.
notes.21:2: The Greek text reads "Dagon" (where the Masoretic Hebrew has "the south") and transliterates "Negeb" as a proper name, describing it as "the chief forest of the Negeb."
notes.21:3: The Greek uses the doubled divine title kyrios Kyrios ("the Lord, the Lord") and reads "from the east to the north" (so also 21:9), whereas the Hebrew has "from south to north."
notes.21:8: The Greek reads "the unrighteous and the lawless" (repeated in 21:9), differing from the Masoretic Hebrew reading "the righteous and the wicked."
notes.21:25: In this Greek critical text, 21:25 repeats the final clause of 21:24 concerning the sword entering against Rabbath, Judea, and Jerusalem; both verses are translated as they stand.
notes.21:32: The Greek repeats "iniquity" three times (where the Masoretic Hebrew reads "ruin" or "overturn") and frames 21:31 with past-tense accusations rather than imperatives.
notes.22:3: Greek enthymemata ("devices" or "inventions") is the Septuagint's characteristic rendering in Ezekiel for the Hebrew term for idols; it is retained literally here and in 22:4.
notes.22:16: The Greek reads "I will take an inheritance in you" (interpreting the Hebrew consonant root as "inherit" in the first person), whereas the Masoretic Text reads "you shall be profaned in yourself."
notes.22:25: The Greek reads "whose leaders" rather than the Masoretic Hebrew "a conspiracy of her prophets."
notes.22:28: The Greek renders "who plaster them shall fall" (relating the Hebrew term for whitewash to the verb "fall"), and in 22:29 places "the people of the land" in the accusative as the victims of oppression rather than its perpetrators.
notes.23:7: Greek enthymemata (literally "devices" or "contrivances") is the Septuagint's characteristic rendering in Ezekiel for idols (also in vv. 30, 37, and 49).
notes.23:15: Greek opsis trisse literally means "a threefold appearance" (compare trissous, "triple-ranked officers," in v. 23), reflecting a literal Greek rendering of the Hebrew military title for officers of the third rank; the clause also ends with the singular "of his birth."
notes.23:20: The Greek text explicitly reads "the Chaldeans" (where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "their paramours") and uses aidoia ("private parts") rather than "emission."
notes.23:23: The Greek preserves the Septuagint proper names Phakouk, Soue, and Hychoue, corresponding to Pekod, Shoa, and Koa in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.23:34: The Septuagint reads "and her feasts and her new moons I will turn away," differing markedly from the Masoretic Text's imagery of draining the cup, gnawing its sherds, and tearing the breasts.
notes.24:7: In the Greek text, the Lord speaks in the first person ("I have set it... I have not poured it"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads third person ("she set it... she did not pour it").
notes.24:9: The Greek text reads "magnify the people" (ton laon), a distinctive Septuagint reading where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "make the woodpile great."
notes.24:17: The Greek reads "a groaning of blood, of the loins, of mourning," reflecting an alternative reading of the Hebrew consonants compared to the Masoretic Text ("sigh silently; make no mourning for the dead").
notes.24:18: The Septuagint omits the notice of the death of Ezekiel's wife found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text, reporting simply that Ezekiel spoke and acted in the morning as commanded.
notes.25:4: "Kedem" transliterates the Hebrew word for "east" as a proper name in the Greek, and "fatness" (pioteta) reflects a different vocalization of the Hebrew word for "milk."
notes.25:9: The Greek renders the Moabite border cities distinctively as "the house of Thasimouth, of the ascent of the city by the sea," differing from the Masoretic Text's Beth-jeshimoth, Baal-meon, and Kiriathaim.
notes.25:12: The Greek uses the Hellenized name "Idumea" for Edom throughout verses twelve through fourteen, and in verse thirteen renders the Hebrew place name Dedan as the participle "those pursued" (diokomenoi).
notes.25:15: "The foreigners" (hoi allophyloi) is the Septuagint's standard designation for the Philistines; in verse sixteen, the Greek likewise identifies the Cherethites as "Cretans" (Kretas).
notes.26:2: The Greek spells Tyre as "Sor" (from Hebrew Tsor), rendered here by its standard English name, and reads "the nations have perished" where the Masoretic Text has "the gates of the peoples."
notes.26:15: Here and in verses nineteen and twenty-one, the Greek reads kyrios Kyrios ("the Lord, the Lord"), corresponding to the double divine title in Hebrew.
notes.26:20: The Greek reads "nor rise up upon the land of life," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "and I will set glory in the land of the living."
notes.27:2: Throughout chapter 27 the Greek text transliterates Tyre as Sor (from Hebrew Tsor), whereas chapter 28 uses the Greek name Tyre.
notes.27:4: The Septuagint reads for Beelim (as a proper name) and your sons, where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has your borders and your builders.
notes.27:12: The Greek text renders Tarshish as Carthaginians here (while transliterating Tarshish in verse 16) and likewise uses distinctive Greek geographical names in this trade list, including Byblos (v. 9), Greece (v. 13), Rhodians (v. 15), and Miletus (v. 18).
notes.27:16: The Septuagint treats Lamoth and Chorchor as proper names (corresponding to coral and ruby in the Hebrew text) and reads men where the Hebrew has Aram; similarly, Asel (v. 19) and Charman (v. 24) reflect distinctive Greek proper-name forms.
notes.27:32: Verse 31 of the Hebrew Masoretic Text is absent in the Septuagint; in verse 32 the Greek also reads their sons where the Hebrew has in their wailing.
notes.28:12: The doubled Greek title kyrios Kyrios ("the Lord, the Lord") reflects Hebrew Adonai YHWH; here and in verse 25 it is rendered literally to preserve the Greek wording.
notes.28:13: The Septuagint lists all twelve stones of the high priest's breastpiece (cf. Exodus 28:17-20) along with silver and gold, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text lists nine stones; the Greek also reads treasuries and storehouses at the end of the verse.
notes.28:14: Reading the Hebrew particle as the preposition with, the Septuagint places the prince of Tyre with the cherub rather than identifying him as an anointed cherub, and in verse 16 depicts the cherub leading him out from the fiery stones.
notes.28:18: The Septuagint has the first-person verb I profaned, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads the second-person you profaned.
notes.29:1: The Greek text dates this oracle to the first day of the tenth month (compare the twelfth day in the Masoretic Text).
notes.29:4: The Greek reads "snares" (pagidas) rather than "hooks," and "fins" literally renders pterygas ("wings" or "fins").
notes.29:7: The Greek distinctively reads "when every hand clapped against them" (compare "you tore all their shoulder" in the Masoretic Text).
notes.29:19: "The Sovereign Lord" renders the Greek double divine title kyrios Kyrios (reflecting Hebrew Adonai YHWH), which recurs in 29:20, 30:10, 13, 22, and 31:15, 18.
notes.30:3: The Greek reads "the end of the nations" (peras ethnon) and omits the phrase "a day of clouds" found in the Masoretic Text.
notes.30:5: The Greek names "Persians and Cretans and Lydians and Libyans" along with "the sons of My covenant" (compare Cush, Put, Lud, and "the land of the covenant" in the Masoretic Text).
notes.30:14: Here and in verses 15-17, the Greek uses Hellenistic names for Egyptian cities: Tanis (Hebrew Zoan), Diospolis (Thebes, Hebrew No), Sais (Hebrew Sin), Syene (Hebrew Sin in 30:16), Heliopolis (Hebrew Aven/On), and Bubastis (Hebrew Pibeseth).
notes.30:16: The Greek closes the verse with "and waters shall be poured out" (compare "and Noph shall have adversaries daily" in the Masoretic Text).
notes.30:24: The Greek has the king of Babylon bringing the sword upon Egypt to plunder and despoil her, where the Masoretic Text speaks of breaking Pharaoh's arms and his groaning.
notes.31:3: Here and in verse 8, the Greek identifies the tree as a "cypress" (kyparissos) rather than a cedar, and places its top "into the midst of the clouds" (nephelon).
notes.31:8: The Greek text opens without a negation ("And such cypresses were in the paradise of God") before contrasting the pine and fir trees with Asshur's shoots and boughs.
notes.31:14: The Greek shifts into the indicative in the middle clauses ("yet they set their top... and they did not stand"), reflecting a literal rendering of difficult underlying syntax.
notes.31:17: The Greek reads "his seed" (sperma) rather than "his arm" and "perished in the midst of their life" (compare "in the midst of the nations" in the Masoretic Text).
notes.32:1: The Greek text dates this oracle to the tenth month, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads the twelfth month.
notes.32:8: The Greek uses the doubled divine title kyrios Kyrios ("the Lord, the Lord"), reflecting the Hebrew Adonai YHWH here and in verses 32:16, 32:31, 32:32, and 33:25.
notes.32:17: The Greek specifies the first month, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text omits the month; verse 32:19 does not stand as a separate verse in the Greek, as its material appears in verse 32:21.
notes.32:21: The Greek reads en bathei thorybou ("in the depth of tumult"), a distinctive textual reading where the Hebrew has "from the midst of Sheol" and some witnesses read bothrou ("pit").
notes.32:29: Here and in verse 32:30, the Greek names Assyria ("the rulers of Assyria" and "commanders of Assyria"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text names Edom in verse 32:29 and the Sidonians in verse 32:30.
notes.33:13: The Greek text omits the clause "that he shall surely live" found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text after "When I say to the righteous man," passing directly to his trust in his own righteousness.
notes.33:21: The Greek dates the fugitive's arrival to the twelfth month, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads the tenth month.
notes.33:25: The Greek text omits the remainder of verse 33:25 and all of verse 33:26 found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text, passing directly from the prophetic formula to the oath in verse 33:27.
notes.33:31: The Greek reads "falsehood" (pseudos) and "defilements" (miasmaton), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text speaks of expressions of affection and dishonest gain.
notes.34:2: The Greek doubles the divine title (kyrios Kyrios, literally "Lord, the Lord"), rendered here as "the Sovereign Lord" to distinguish it from simple Kyrios ("the Lord") and Kyrios ho theos ("the Lord God"). The Greek also opens with the address "O shepherds" and a rhetorical question rather than the Masoretic Hebrew "Woe to the shepherds... who feed themselves."
notes.34:3: The Greek reads "the milk" (to gala) rather than the Masoretic Hebrew "the fat," reflecting a different vocalization of the Hebrew consonants.
notes.34:4: The Greek uses the rare verb somatopoieo ("restore to bodily health") and concludes "you wore down the strong with toil," where the Masoretic Hebrew speaks of ruling the flock with force and harshness.
